% Figure: the moment threshold as a dial. Referenced from §8 after prop:bessel-family.
% Generated by scripts/make-fig-families.py (inverse-gamma / Bessel family across the shape
% a, with the Gamma kernel for contrast). Design after the hub's covariant_memory_figure.py.
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig-families.png}
\caption{The moment threshold, seen in the tails. Left, log--log: the kernels $\phi_1$ of the
Bessel family of Proposition~\ref{prop:bessel-family} for shapes $a = \tfrac12, 1, 2, 4$ are
straight lines of slope $-(a+1)$ at large $t$, so the moments of order $n < a$ are finite and
no others; $a = \tfrac12$ is the extremal stable member of the semigroup theory, the heaviest
tail in the family, with no mean. The dashed curve is the Gamma kernel with $\gamma = 2$: an
exponential tail, every moment finite (Proposition~\ref{prop:gamma-moments}). Right: the same
kernels on a linear scale at unit canonical scale. Raising $a$ buys moments at the price of
temporal reach --- a heavier tail is a longer scale-invariant memory, not a defect. The
comparison at matched delay, which is what an implementation sees, is in \S\ref{sec:implementation}.}
\label{fig:families}
\end{figure}
